newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ may act if monetary conditions stay tight-ANZ.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ may act if monetary conditions stay tight-ANZ.

text.p: If New Zealand monetary conditions remain around current levels after the release on Tuesday of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), the Reserve Bank is likely to take some action, ANZ Bank said on Monday.

With the recent strengthening of the New Zealand dollar and its Trade-Weighted Index countered by only limited falls in bill rates, ANZ said monetary conditions had tightened to levels close to those prevailing when the RBNZ last eased.

"Current conditions are close to the levels prevailing in the period immediately prior to the release of the March Economic Projections that the RBNZ considered too tight," ANZ said in its weekly Market Focus.
"Indeed, we consider the only thing holding back the RBNZ from taking action at this time is the upcoming CPI release.
"However, should the result be in line with expectations and monetary conditions remain around current levels, then we would expect the RBNZ to take some action."
One way or another, ANZ said it expected some easing in monetary conditions from current levels.

On the basis of 90-day bill rates of 7.7 percent and a TWI of 68.8 (at the time of writing last week), ANZ said 90-day rates would have to fall almost 75 basis points or the TWI around 100 points for monetary conditions to be equivalent to the RBNZ's policy call.
ANZ said it was touch more optimistic than the Reserve Bank that Tuesday's CPI would include more encouraging signs on the inflation front.
"We expect underlying inflation to be 0.4 percent in the March quarter, taking the annual rate down to 2.2 percent from 2.4 percent in the December year," the bank said.
Headline inflation was expected to be 0.1 percent for the quarter and 2.2 percent for the year to March.

"A March quarter CPI result in line with our expectations may provide much needed reassurance to the financial markets that New Zealand is on track to achieve lower inflation over the year ahead," ANZ said.

"Regardless of the impact of increased government spending on the longer term inflation outlook, it may cause the markets to question why monetary conditions are tighter than the RBNZ requires at this time.
"This could lead to some retracement in short rates and/or the New Zealand dollar."
